lede: Bitcoin broke below $70,000 overnight for the first time since August, triggering more than $1.3bn of crypto liquidations as Fed-hike bets and a 19-month dollar high squeezed risk. Gold is clawing back above $3,900 after Thursday's 3% drop, with US October PPI the main data test today.

focus.text: Up about 1% near $3,915 after Thursday's 3% slide to a near one-year low around $3,852; sitting just above its $3,910 pivot. US PPI at 16:30 TRT is the key risk.
Flat near 1.1058, below its 1.1067 pivot, with the dollar index around 103.2 on December hike pricing. Eurozone Q3 GDP (13:00) and US PPI (16:30) are today's tests.

technicals.indicators: Thursday's low held at the 0.786 Fib (~3,850) · 127.2% extension at 3,794 · price just above pivot 3,910
technicals.note: Gold broke its late-October low near $3,870 and is now bouncing inside a falling channel; $4,000 remains the level that capped the latest recovery.

technicals.indicators: RSI near oversold · below 100-day SMA · Elliott count: wave-4 high at 1.127
technicals.note: The pair is trading at the lower end of a five-wave decline from the early-November high, with the 1.1100 break still unrepaired.

technicals.indicators: Broke 1.3271 support · medium-term uptrend intact while above 1.3008
technicals.note: Cable is at a four-week low despite strong UK Q3 GDP, with the rebound from 1.3135 now viewed as a completed correction.

technicals.indicators: RSI ≈ 33 before the latest drop · below key MAs (≈77.3k–80.9k) · trading below pivot 72,167
technicals.note: Bitcoin lost the $70,000 floor to its lowest since August and is on course for a sixth straight weekly decline.

technicals.indicators: RSI ≈ 28 (oversold) on Thursday · below MAs at ≈2,238–2,429
technicals.note: Ether slipped under $2,000 for the first time since August, extending a sequence of lower highs since its last bounce.

news.text: Futures now price roughly 85–89% odds of a quarter-point Fed hike on 9 Dec, and about 11% for a half-point move after the hot October CPI.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned with immediate effect, CFO Colette Kress steps in; the stock lost 4.3% and the S&P 500 slipped 0.35% to 7,592.
Brent settled 3.3% higher at $95.82 after Houthi claims of strikes on Saudi energy sites and Iranian reports of tankers hit near Hormuz.
Gold fell about 3% on Thursday to its lowest in roughly a year as the dollar index hit a 19-month high above 103; silver dropped under $50.
UK GDP grew 0.7% in Q3, but sterling still slid to a four-week low near 1.32 as Fed-hike expectations dominated.
Bitcoin slid below $70,000 to about $69,000, its lowest since mid-August, and is down roughly 17% this quarter.
Over $1.3bn of futures positions were wiped out in 24 hours per Coinglass, $677m in bitcoin; one $31m BTC long on Hyperliquid was the largest.
US spot bitcoin ETFs saw $300m of net outflows on 11 Nov, a fifth straight day (~$1.44bn total); BlackRock's IBIT has bled for nine sessions. Ether ETFs lost $145m.
Ether dropped under $2,000 for the first time since August, while SOL fell below $80 and XRP hovered around $1.
MSCI's removal of Strategy after 30 Nov keeps pressure on: JPMorgan sees about $2.8bn of passive selling, up to $8.8bn if other index providers follow.
A Zcash draft proposal would pull 50,000 ZEC from the community grants treasury; holders vote from 16 to 30 Nov.
